how_to_obtain.instruction: In the MDM console, navigate to Configuration Profiles and look for profiles of type 'SCEP', 'PKCS Certificate', 'Trusted Certificate', or 'Certificate'. Verify at least one certificate profile is active and assigned. In Intune: Devices > Configuration Profiles, filter by profile type 'SCEP certificate' or 'PKCS certificate'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune: Devices > Configuration Profiles (filter: Certificate profiles) | Jamf Pro: Configuration Profiles > Certificate payload | Workspace ONE: Profiles > Credentials payload
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more certificate profiles with status 'Active' and assigned to device groups. Profile details should show a valid CA, renewal threshold, and subject name format.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the MDM API for configuration profiles filtered to certificate profile types. Confirm that SCEP or PKCS profiles exist in an active, assigned state. Also verify the certificate authority connector is configured and healthy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response includes certificate profile objects with `assignments` populated. An empty response or profiles with no assignments indicates certificate provisioning is not active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a managed device, check the device certificate store for certificates issued by the corporate CA. On iOS/macOS check via Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > [MDM Profile] > More Details. On Windows, use certlm.msc to inspect the Personal and MDM certificate stores.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where-Object {$_.Issuer -like '*YourCorpCA*'} | Select-Object Subject, NotAfter, Thumbprint
how_to_obtain.navigation: iOS: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > [Profile] > More Details | Windows: certlm.msc > Personal > Certificates
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Certificate issued by the corporate CA with a future expiration date and auto-renewal configured. Absence of corporate-issued certificates indicates provisioning is not working.

option_description: Specifies how frequently (in hours) the MDM platform actively re-evaluates whether device configurations still match the deployed security profiles and re-pushes or re-applies profiles when configuration drift is detected. This controls how quickly unauthorized changes to device settings (VPN removed, Wi-Fi changed, certificate deleted) are detected and remediated.
security_impact: The Rego policy `over_the_air_configuration_management` requires this value to be 24 hours or less. A check frequency exceeding 24 hours creates windows where devices with removed or tampered security configurations continue operating in a degraded security state. For example, a user who removes the VPN configuration profile may have unrestricted internet access for days before re-enforcement occurs, bypassing traffic inspection and data loss prevention controls.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the MDM console, locate the device check-in schedule or compliance evaluation interval. In Intune this is found under Tenant Administration > Enrollment restrictions or the device check-in policy. In Jamf Pro, check Settings > Computer Management > Check-In to view the management framework check-in interval.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune: Tenant Administration > Device check-in settings | Jamf Pro: Settings > Computer Management Framework > Check-In | Workspace ONE: Groups & Settings > All Settings > Devices & Users > General > Agent Settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A check-in interval of 24 hours or less (e.g., 'Every 8 hours', 'Every 15 minutes') indicates adequate configuration drift detection frequency.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the MDM API for device management check-in configuration and review the lastSyncDateTime across a sample of managed devices to derive actual observed check-in intervals versus configured intervals.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: lastSyncDateTime values for all active devices should be within the configured check interval. Devices with lastSyncDateTime older than 24 hours indicate check-in is failing or configured infrequently.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review MDM server-side logs or device telemetry to calculate the actual observed check-in interval from a sample of devices. Compare this to the configured policy value to detect discrepancies between policy and reality.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries showing regular check-in events per device with timestamps no more than the configured interval apart. Gaps exceeding 24 hours are flagged.

option_description: Controls whether the MDM platform is actively recording a comprehensive audit trail of security-relevant events, including device enrollment and removal, policy creation and modification, compliance state changes, administrator actions, and remote commands (wipe, lock, reset). This is the master switch for MDM audit logging functionality.
security_impact: The Rego policy `audit_logging_and_event_completeness` requires `audit_logging_enabled` to be `true` as an absolute prerequisite. Without audit logging, there is no forensic record of MDM administrator actions, no visibility into when devices were remotely wiped or locked, and no audit trail for compliance investigations or incident response. This control is foundational for detecting insider threats (unauthorized remote wipes) and demonstrating compliance with regulatory frameworks requiring access logs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the MDM admin console, navigate to Settings or Administration and locate Audit Logs, Logging, or Monitoring configuration. In Microsoft Intune, check Tenant Administration > Audit Logs to verify logs are being captured. In Jamf Pro, check Settings > System Settings > Log Flushing and the built-in Management History.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune: Tenant Administration > Audit Logs (verify entries exist and are current) | Jamf Pro: Settings > System Settings > Log Flushing | Workspace ONE: Monitor > Reports & Analytics > Audit Logs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit log console showing recent events (within last 24 hours) across multiple event categories. An empty audit log or a 'logging disabled' indicator confirms the control is not active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the MDM audit log API endpoint and verify that recent events are being captured. A successful response with recent timestamped log entries confirms logging is enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response with an array of recent audit events. An empty `value` array when activity has occurred, or a 404/403 indicating the endpoint is unavailable, suggests logging is disabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether MDM audit logs are being forwarded to the SIEM or centralized logging platform. Query the SIEM for MDM-sourced events to confirm the pipeline is active and logs are flowing.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -X GET 'https://api.securitycenter.microsoft.com/api/activities?filter=source eq MDM' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -c 'activityDateTime'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SIEM query returns recent MDM events with valid timestamps. Zero results when MDM activity has occurred confirms logging is disabled or the forwarding pipeline is broken.

option_description: Defines the specific categories of events that the MDM system is configured to capture in its audit log. Expected categories include device_enrollment, policy_changes, compliance_events, admin_actions, remote_commands, and authentication. Gaps in this list mean entire classes of security-relevant activity leave no audit trail.
security_impact: The Rego policy `audit_logging_and_event_completeness` requires all four of these categories to be present: `policy_changes`, `admin_actions`, `compliance_events`, and `remote_commands`. Missing any one of these creates a specific forensic blind spot — absent `remote_commands` logging means unauthorized remote wipes cannot be investigated; absent `policy_changes` logging means policy tampering by a rogue admin is undetectable; absent `compliance_events` means the audit cannot demonstrate that enforcement was active at the time of an incident.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the MDM console audit log or logging settings, review the list of enabled event categories or event types. In Microsoft Intune, navigate to Tenant Administration > Audit Logs and use the Activity Type filter dropdown to enumerate available and active categories. In Jamf Pro, review Management History and Log Flushing settings for available log types.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Intune: Tenant Administration > Audit Logs > Filter by Activity Type | Jamf Pro: Settings > System Settings > Log Flushing | Workspace ONE: Monitor > Audit Logs > Event Category filter
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Filter dropdown or settings page showing enabled categories including: device enrollment/unenrollment, policy create/update/delete, compliance state change, admin sign-in, remote actions (wipe/lock/reset).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the MDM audit log API across each expected event category to verify that events of each type are present in the log. If a category returns zero results despite known activity, that category is not being logged.
how_to_obtain.command: for category in 'Enrollment' 'CompliancePolicy' 'DeviceAction' 'PolicySet' 'Authentication'; do echo "=== $category ==="; curl -s "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/auditEvents?\$filter=category eq '$category'&\$top=1" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' | python3 -m json.tool | grep 'activityDateTime'; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each category query returns at least one recent event with a valid activityDateTime. Categories returning empty results despite known activity are not being logged.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If MDM logs are forwarded to a SIEM, query the SIEM to enumerate distinct event categories present in MDM log data over the past 30 days. Compare the discovered categories against the required list to identify gaps.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=mdm | stats count by event_category | sort -count' OR elk query: GET /mdm-logs-*/_search -d '{"aggs":{"categories":{"terms":{"field":"event_category.keyword"}}},"size":0}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SIEM aggregation results showing all six expected categories (device_enrollment, policy_changes, compliance_events, admin_actions, remote_commands, authentication) with non-zero event counts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Perform a controlled test for each required event category: enroll a test device (device_enrollment), modify a compliance policy (policy_changes), trigger a remote lock (remote_commands), and observe an admin sign-in (authentication). Verify each action generates a corresponding audit log entry.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each test action produces a matching audit log entry within 5 minutes, confirming that the event category is actively logged. Missing log entries for any test action identify uncovered categories.

option_description: Controls the number of days that MDM audit logs are retained in the system before they are deleted or archived. This setting governs the lifecycle of all recorded MDM events including policy changes, administrator actions, compliance events, device enrollment/unenrollment records, and remote command execution history.
security_impact: The Rego policy rule 'audit_logging_and_event_completeness' requires log_retention_days >= 90 as a mandatory condition for the countermeasure to be credited. Without meeting this threshold, even a fully enabled audit logging configuration will fail the policy check. Insufficient retention undermines forensic investigations (e.g., tracing a data breach involving a managed device), prevents compliance reporting against PCI-DSS (90 days minimum), HIPAA (6 years), and SOC 2 requirements, and eliminates the ability to reconstruct administrator action timelines after a security incident. A retention value of 0 effectively means logs are purged immediately, rendering audit logging functionally useless.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Intune: Navigate to the Microsoft Endpoint Manager Admin Center (endpoint.microsoft.com), go to Tenant Administration > Diagnostics > Audit Logs, then check the retention policy displayed or navigate to Tenant Administration > Tenant Status > Connector Status for log configuration details. For other MDM platforms such as Jamf Pro, navigate to Settings > System Settings > Log Management or Logs to find the retention policy configuration.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft Intune: endpoint.microsoft.com > Tenant Administration > Diagnostics > Audit Logs | Jamf Pro: Settings > System Settings > Log Management
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric value displayed indicating the configured retention period in days, such as '90 days', '180 days', or '365 days'. If no value is shown, the platform may be using a default or the retention may not be explicitly configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Microsoft Graph API to retrieve the Intune device management audit log retention configuration. Authenticate with an admin token and call the auditEvents endpoint to inspect available log age, or query the deviceManagement settings endpoint. For Jamf Pro, use the Jamf Pro REST API to query /api/v1/settings/obj/applicationSettings for logging configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -X GET 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/deviceManagement/auditEvents?$top=1&$orderby=activityDateTime desc' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | python3 -m json.tool
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON response containing audit event records with activityDateTime fields. Compare the oldest log timestamp to the current date to infer effective retention. For direct policy queries, expect a JSON field such as 'retentionDays' or equivalent with a numeric value.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For MDM platforms with PowerShell management modules (e.g., Microsoft Intune via Microsoft.Graph PowerShell SDK), use the following commands to retrieve the log retention configuration programmatically. This provides a scriptable, repeatable method suitable for compliance audits.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All'; $auditEvents = Get-MgDeviceManagementAuditEvent -Top 1 -Sort 'activityDateTime desc'; $oldestEvent = Get-MgDeviceManagementAuditEvent -Top 1 -Sort 'activityDateTime asc'; $retentionDays = [math]::Round(((Get-Date) - [datetime]$oldestEvent.ActivityDateTime).TotalDays); Write-Output "Effective log retention (days): $retentionDays"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric output such as 'Effective log retention (days): 180' indicating how many days of audit log history are currently accessible. A value below 90 indicates non-compliance with the Rego policy condition.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the MDM platform administrator or review the documented MDM operational runbook to identify whether a log retention policy has been formally configured, whether logs are archived to an external SIEM or log management platform (e.g., Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic), and what the documented retention target is. Request evidence such as a screenshot of the MDM console retention setting, a SIEM data retention policy document, or a storage lifecycle policy for log archives.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Written documentation or verbal confirmation specifying the retention period in days (e.g., '365 days retained in MDM console, then archived to Splunk for 2 years'). Absence of documentation or a value below 90 days should be flagged as a finding.

typical_values: 0 (critical risk — logs purged immediately or no retention configured)
